reference_sql:
-- Step 1: one row per registered customer. Step 2: one row in total.
SELECT ROUND(AVG(t.n_stores), 2) AS avg_stores
FROM (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT store_id) AS n_stores
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
) AS t
alternatives:
WITH customer_stores AS (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT store_id) AS n_stores
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(n_stores), 2) AS avg_stores
FROM customer_stores

SELECT ROUND(AVG(t.n_stores), 2) AS avg_stores
FROM (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT pairs.customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_stores
  FROM (
    -- one row per registered customer and store
    SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, store_id
    FROM orders
    WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  ) AS pairs
  GROUP BY pairs.customer_id
) AS t

other_way.sql:
WITH customer_stores AS (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT store_id) AS n_stores
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(n_stores), 2) AS avg_stores
FROM customer_stores
other_way.tradeoff: A WITH step names the per-customer store counts before the average, which reads top to bottom but takes a few more lines.
